rounds.text: Permanent Magnets Ltd is displaying exceptional top-line and bottom-line acceleration, evidenced by compounded sales growth of 31% [E14] and compounded profit growth of 51% [E17 (Wait, E15 is profit growth)] over the trailing twelve months [E14, E15]. This momentum is powerfully reinforced by quarterly performance, with operating margin surging to 24% in September 2026 compared to 12% in the year-ago quarter, marking an 11 percentage point expansion [E23]. Furthermore, profit growth heavily outperforms recent price action, with profit growth exceeding 1-year price growth by 44%, signaling that the company is starting to outperform market expectations [E44]. Operational execution is sound, highlighted by a strong cash conversion of 1.20x for March 2026 where operating cash flow of Rs 18 Cr fully backs reported profits [E26, E27], alongside a comfortable current ratio of 4.06x [E30]. Future growth catalysts are actively building, as Capital Work in Progress (CWIP) has risen by 237.5% to Rs 27 Cr as of September 2026, demonstrating active capital deployment [E32]. Conceded: [E37], [E38], [E55], [E56].

Permanent Magnets Ltd carries an extreme valuation that completely disconnects from both its fundamental returns and quantitative intrinsic value models [E56]. The stock trades at an exorbitant P/E of 47.9x to 53.38x, vastly exceeding the sector benchmark of 21.3x, alongside a hefty P/B of 5.25x to 5.62x against a 2.39x sector average [E1, E2, E6, E7]. This aggressive pricing is further underscored by a discounted cash flow intrinsic value estimate of Rs 475 per share, creating a negative margin of safety of -114.7% at the current market price of Rs 1,019 [E2, E37, E38]. Furthermore, a reverse DCF reveals that today's market price aggressively prices in 20.5% earnings growth, whereas the baseline case assumes only 10.0% [E39]. Operational and cash flow metrics also show notable vulnerabilities, including a severe negative free cash flow of Rs -26 Cr in March 2026, rising borrowings, inconsistent operating margins, and flags regarding potential interest capitalization [E24, E28, E31, E49]. conceded: [E14, E15, E26, E30]

conceded: [E37, E38, E39, E49]. The bear's fixation on multiples like the 47.9x to 53.38x P/E [E1, E6] and 5.25x to 5.62x P/B [E2, E7] ignores that the company is experiencing a fundamental earnings explosion, with compounded profit growth at 51% [E15] and a recent quarterly profit surge of 217% YoY [E53]. The negative free cash flow of Rs -26 Cr in March 2026 [E28] and rising borrowings [E31] are entirely natural manifestations of a massive capital expenditure build-up phase, evidenced by Capital Work in Progress surging 237.5% to Rs 27 Cr [E32]. While operating margins have historical inconsistencies [E24], the most recent data shows a dramatic expansion to 24% in September 2026 compared to 12% in the year-ago quarter [E23], complemented by stellar 31% trailing sales growth [E14] and cash-backed profits showing a 1.20x cash conversion ratio [E26]. Finally, dismissing the stock on stale sentiment or technical averages misses that profit growth is currently exceeding 1-year price growth by 44% with a ratio of 7.29, signaling that the company is rapidly starting to outperform expectations [E44, E57].

The bull leans heavily on explosive profit growth of 51% [E15] and a 217% YoY quarterly surge [E53], but this performance masks an inconsistent operating-margin trend over both the last three years and the last three quarters [E24, E25]. Conceded: the company shows a recent quarterly operating margin expansion to 24% [E23] and a 1.20x cash conversion ratio [E26]. However, this positive operational window fails to justify a valuation where a reverse DCF requires an aggressive 20.5% earnings growth rate [E39], especially when the stock is already trading below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E42]. The bull dismisses negative free cash flow of Rs -26 Cr [E28] and rising borrowings of Rs 92 Cr [E31] as mere manifestations of a 237.5% surge in CWIP [E32], yet filed statements explicitly flag a structural risk that the company might be capitalizing interest costs [E49]. Furthermore, citing a 44% outperformance of profit growth over price growth [E44] ignores that institutional ownership has completely vanished with foreign institutions holding 0.00% and domestic institutions holding a negligible 0.01% [E34, E35].
